page: Microsoft Azure E64as_v4 is a memory-optimized virtual machine belonging to the EASv4 server family. It is powered by an AMD EPYC 7763 processor with an x86_64 architecture, offering 64 dedicated vCPUs across 32 physical cores with multithreading enabled. The system features a 3.525 GHz clock speed, 512 GB of RAM providing 8 GB per core, and a local 885 GB SSD. It runs on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor and supports Premium Storage.

Benchmark data indicates strong multi-core and memory performance. The server achieves top-tier results in Passmark memory testing and strong scores in multi-core stress-ng, Passmark CPU, and Geekbench multi-core benchmarks. Database operations are highly efficient, with Redis SET operations reaching 62.62 million operations per second. However, while cached memory bandwidth is strong at 4162.87 GB/sec, uncached read and write memory bandwidths fall into the average category.

Due to the lack of GPU acceleration, the server is poorly suited for large-scale AI tasks, as demonstrated by its weak performance of 2.76 tokens per second in large-model LLM text generation. It is, however, highly cost-effective for memory-intensive enterprise workloads that do not require accelerators. The hardware profile is optimized for relational databases, in-memory caching systems like Redis, software compilation, and data-dense general-purpose applications.
description: Microsoft Azure E64as_v4 is an x86_64 memory-optimized virtual machine powered by a dedicated AMD EPYC 7763 processor. It features 64 vCPUs, 32 physical cores, 512 GB of RAM, and an 885 GB local SSD. Operating on Microsoft Hyper-V, this server delivers strong multi-core processing and top-tier memory performance, as evidenced by high Passmark memory scores and 62.62 million Redis SET operations per second. While cached memory bandwidth is strong, uncached memory bandwidth remains average. Additionally, the lack of a GPU results in weak performance for large-scale LLM text generation. This server is highly cost-efficient for memory-intensive workloads, making it best suited for database hosting, in-memory caching, and large-scale software compilation.
